description: GOBACK itself is a 2002 introduction; a GOBACK RETURNING is gated by goback-returning-2002 (its more-specific 0900 subsumes this row - the pass fires this row only for a BARE GOBACK). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 ends a run unit with STOP RUN, 'If the RUN phrase is specified, execution of the run unit ceases and control is transferred to the operating system.' (§1985:VI.6.24.4 GR1), and a called program with EXIT PROGRAM, 'The EXIT PROGRAM statement marks the logical end of a called program.' (§1985:X.5.4.1), and has no GOBACK; 2002 adds 'The GOBACK statement marks the logical end of a function, a method, or a program.' (§2002:14.8.17), §2002:F.1 item 6 lists GOBACK under 'Reserved words. The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 62: 'GOBACK statement. A GOBACK statement has been added that always returns control, either to the operating system or to the calling runtime element.' §2014:14.9.17 and §2023:14.9.18.1 carry the 2002 sentence. Folded from the inline CallBinder gate (Exec Step E).
